title: Crispy Ginger Beef
subtitle: Calgary's takeout classic made mild: crisp strips of beef with carrots in a sticky ginger-garlic glaze
imageAlt: Crispy beef strips and carrot matchsticks in a dark glossy ginger glaze beside rice in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Freeze the steak 20 minutes so it slices into thin, even strips.
Start the rice first. This version is mild, with no chili at all.

items.name: sirloin steak
items.note: sliced across the grain in 5 mm strips

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Toss the beef with the salt and egg, then with the cornstarch until every strip is coated and dry-looking.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet or wok over medium-high to about 180°C (350°F). Fry the beef in 3 batches, separating the strips, 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp, far past 63°C (145°F). Drain on a rack.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the carrots and onion 2 minutes, add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then the brown sugar, soy sauce, vinegar and water. Bring to a boil, stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer 1 minute until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Toss the beef in the glaze and serve right away over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Slice thinner, and don't crowd the oil; fry in smaller batches.
Drop them into the oil one by one and stir after 30 seconds.
Loosen with a spoon of water before tossing.

saleTip: Sirloin or inside round on sale works; inside round is often cheaper and fine sliced thin and fried.
swap: Inside round or flank steak: same amount, sliced thin across the grain.
leftovers: Re-crisp in the air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 4–5 minutes.
doneness: Thin strips are fried well done, far past Health Canada's 63°C (145°F) minimum for whole cuts of beef; coating deep golden.
source: Based on tested Calgary-style ginger beef methods (Canadian Living, Calgary Herald recipe archives): egg-and-cornstarch coated beef strips shallow-fried crisp, tossed in a ginger, garlic, soy and brown sugar glaze, chili omitted.
prepAhead: Slice the beef and cut the vegetables up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: Air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 4–5 minutes, or in a hot skillet, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Crispy beef in a soy-brown sugar-garlic glaze, no fresh ginger or vegetables.

stepNotes.3: Basic: skip the vegetables and ginger; start with the garlic.

fancy.note: Extra crisp with a double fry, finished with sesame.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: after all batches, fry everything again together 1 minute for extra crunch.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: stir in the sesame oil with the cornstarch.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Scatter the sesame seeds over the beef.

plating: Beef piled high next to the rice.

why.0-2: The egg and cornstarch coating is what turns into the shatter-crisp crust.
why.1-6: Vinegar keeps the sticky glaze tangy so it isn't just sweet.

funFact: Ginger beef was invented in the 1970s at the Silver Inn in Calgary and is now on Chinese-Canadian menus across the country.
pairs: fried rice on the side for a takeout night
